subject: How to use rstan/matlab stan to do MCMC properly

messages.author: 7df0230b2510b8fa
messages.subject: How to use rstan/matlab stan to do MCMC properly
parts:
Hi, I am trying to sample theta* from a function of posterior, something like exp[c*xi(theta|D)]*xi(theta), where xi(theta) is the prior and xi(theta|D) is the posterior.

I am wondering if there is any package in STAN I can use to sample from it properly?

I am very new to STAN so it would be great if you can tell me where to start or if I am looking at the right tool.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to use rstan/matlab stan to do MCMC properly
parts:
Hi,

In Stan, you're declaring / defining:
- D in the data and transformed data blocks
- theta in parameters and transformed parmeters blocks
- log p(D, theta) in the model block
- f(theta, D) where f is any function or even a random number generator in the generated quantities block

On Apr 8, 2016, at 3:16 AM, Zuhe Zhang <zhang...@gmail.com> wrote:


Hi, I am trying to sample theta* from a function of posterior, something like exp[c*xi(theta|D)]*xi(theta), where xi(theta) is the prior and xi(theta|D) is the posterior.

I am wondering if there is any package in STAN I can use to sample from it properly?
Yes, it's Stan.
I am very new to STAN so it would be great if you can tell me where to start or if I am looking at the right tool.

--

Thanks!

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to use rstan/matlab stan to do MCMC properly
parts:
The Stan modeling language allows you to specify (possibly) conditional
probability distributions,

p( parameters | data),

and then estimates expectations

E[f] = \int f(parameters) p( parameters | data) d(parameters).

The names “parameters” and “data” are indicative of our usual Bayesian
applications but they could refer to anything.

I am hesitant that you are defining a well-posed target distribution,
but if that’s really want you want to do then just define that distribution
in the model block and Stan will do the rest.

On Apr 15, 2016, at 7:01 AM, Zuhe Zhang <zhang...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks Bob. My previous questions are a bit confusing. What I am trying to implement here is just a mechanism.  

Let me ask better questions:

1. What does "random number generation" actually mean in Stan?

2. Not necessarily related to posterior sampling, if the goal is simply to sample from an unnormalised density. 
So we could even do rejection sampling, if we can't do it all ourselves, is there an easy way to used Stan to sample from a unnormalised density?

Cheers,


Zuhe

In other words, a Stan program defines an unnormalized log density
that is proportional to p(params | data), usually by defining
the joint density p(params, data) and relying on Bayes's rule that
says p(params | data) prop-to p(params, data) when data is fixed.

- Bob
